title: Normalized compact ideal-power quotient cone
statement: Let R be a compact Hausdorff commutative topological ring, I an ideal, with every R/I^n finite and discrete. Assume the quotient maps jointly separate points. Using the quotient tower and constant-section maps of [def-pe-completed-coefficient-comparison-data], there exists a cone rho from the condensed R ring to the constant quotient rings, normalized on constant sections by the actual quotient maps. For every scheme X its image under p_X^* is limiting and its diagram is naturally isomorphic to the constant quotient diagram on X. For every scheme map f:X→Y, f^* of that cone over Y is still limiting.

proof.text: Use the proved generic compact-tower helpers completedTowerTotallyDisconnected and completedRingTowerLimit in Sheaf.Paper.CompletedCondensedCoefficients. Apply them to Q(n)=R/I^n, the actual quotient maps, and the actual quotient transitions, including n=0. Compactness, joint separation, and surjectivity give precisely the represented continuous-coefficient cone as a limit after pullback to each scheme. normalizedSequenceCompIso identifies mapping the sequence with the sequence of mapped transitions.

The explicit finite constant-function isomorphism completedFinitePointIso gives normalizedFiniteIso as an isomorphism of ring objects, using the equality between transported constant monoid structures and sheafified constant ring structures. The sheafification adjunction proves normalizedConstants_naturality for arbitrary continuous ring maps. This makes the finite comparisons a natural isomorphism normalizedTowerIso between the constant quotient diagram and the continuous quotient diagram. Postcompose the canonical continuous reduction cone with its inverse to construct normalizedQuotientCone. Cancelling each finite comparison proves that its legs precomposed with constant sections are the specified quotient reductions.

Transport the limiting continuous cone through normalizedTowerIso after applying the monoidal point inverse image. The monoidal constantSchemeIso identifies the pulled-back constant quotient diagram with the constant diagram on X. For a scheme map f:X to Y, the monoidal upperStarFromPointComp comparison identifies the composite ring-object pullback with the point pullback to X. IsLimit.mapConeEquiv and mapConeMapCone therefore transfer the known limit over X to the actual nested mapped cone over Y. No preservation of arbitrary inverse limits is asserted.

lean.statement:
theorem sfb_normalized_integral_quotient_cone (R : Type) [CommRing R]
    [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [CompactSpace R] [T2Space R]
    (I : Ideal R) [∀ n : ℕ, Finite (R ⧸ I ^ n)]
    [∀ n : ℕ, DiscreteTopology (R ⧸ I ^ n)]
    (hsep : ∀ x y : R,
      (∀ n : ℕ, Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n) x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n) y) → x = y) :
    ∃ ρ : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj (Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} R)) ⟶
        sfbCoefficientQuotientTower R I ⋙ sfbPointConstantRing,
      (∀ n : ℕ, sfbConstantToContinuous R ≫ (ρ.app (op n)).hom =
        (constantSheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}).map
          (AddCommGrpCat.ofHom
            (ULift.ringEquiv.symm.toRingHom.comp
              ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)).comp ULift.ringEquiv.toRingHom)).toAddMonoidHom)) ∧
      (∀ X : Scheme.{u},
        Nonempty (IsLimit ((upperStarFromPoint X).mapMon.mapCone
          (Cone.mk (Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj R)) ρ))) ∧
        Nonempty ((sfbCoefficientQuotientTower R I ⋙ sfbPointConstantRing ⋙
          (upperStarFromPoint X).mapMon) ≅
            (sfbCoefficientQuotientTower R I ⋙ sfbConstantRing X))) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y),
        Nonempty (IsLimit ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} f).mapMon.mapCone
          ((upperStarFromPoint Y).mapMon.mapCone
            (Cone.mk (Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj R)) ρ)))))
